overview.body:
**Maitreya** ​(*maitreya*) — ‌Future Buddha, ‌Loving-Kindness ​· 'The ​Benevolent ​One' — ​the Bodhisattva ​who ‌will return ​as ​the future ‌Buddha — ​belongs ‌to the ​Buddhist ‌tradition, where ​it is ​catalogued ​under the ​domain ​"Future Buddha, ‌Loving-Kindness". The ​name ‌means "'The ​Benevolent ‌One' — ​the Bodhisattva ‌who ​will return ‌as ​the future ​Buddha".

**Maitreya** ‌is ‌future buddha, ‌loving-kindness. ​The name ​means "'The ‌Benevolent ​One' — ​the ‌Bodhisattva who ​will return ​as ‌the future ​Buddha" ‌and belongs ​to the ​buddhist ​tradition.

PuniCodex ​restores ‌the name ‌as **Maitreya** ​and ‌serves its ​temple ​at [its ‌temple](https://punicodex.com/maitreya/). The ‌restoration ‌needs no ‌distinctive ​letters or ‌diacritics its ​ASCII ​form would ​lose, ‌which places ​the name ​in ​Tier 2. ‌The ​plain ASCII ​form *maitreya* ​survives ‌as a ​modern ‌convenience imposed ​by the ‌early ​domain-name system; ‌the ‌restoration, not ​the fallback, ​is ​the form ​the ‌project defends ‌as philologically ​complete.

the-name.body:
The ​name is ‌attested ‌in Devanagari ​as **मैत्रेय**. ​Etymologically ​it means ​"'The ​Benevolent One' ‌— ​the Bodhisattva ​who will ‌return ​as the ‌future ​Buddha".

The ‌ASCII ​form *maitreya* ​survives only ​because ​the early ​domain-name ‌system could ​not ‌carry diacritics; ​it ‌is a ​technological compromise, ‌not ​an ancient ‌spelling. ​The Unicode ​restoration ‌**Maitreya** recovers ‌the full ‌diacritic ​detail of ​the ‌scholarly transliteration ​directly ​in the ‌address bar. ​The ​restoration needs ‌no ​distinctive letters ‌or ​diacritics its ​ASCII form ​would ​lose, which ‌places ‌the name ​in ‌Tier 2.

​The letter-by-letter ​transformation ‌runs:

- ‌**m** ‌→ **M** ‌— ​Same, capitalized
‌- **a** ​→ ​**a** — ​Same
‌- **i** ​→ ​**i** — ​Same
‌- **t** ​→ **t** ​— ​Same
- ‌**r** ​→ **r** ‌— ​Same
- ‌**e** → ​**e** ‌— Same
‌- ​**y** → ​**y** ​— Same
​- **a** ‌→ ‌**a** — ​Same

pronunciation.body:
The ​reconstructed ‌pronunciation of ‌the ​name ​is ​**/maitreya/** — ​Restored ​scholarly ‌form.

​Phoneme by ​phoneme:

‌- ​**maitreya** ‌— ​The canonical ‌restored ​form ​Maitreya.

​For the ​modern ​speaker, ‌the ​closest approximation ‌is: ​Say ‌"maitreya" ​with the ‌stress ​and ‌length ​implied by ​the ‌scholarly ‌restoration ‌"Maitreya".

​The ASCII ​form ‌"maitreya" ​is ​a DNS ‌compromise; ​the ​restoration ‌"Maitreya" preserves ​the ‌name's ​scholarly ​dignity.

The ​pronunciation ​given ‌above ‌reconstructs the ​sound ‌world ​in ​which ‌Maitreya was ‌invoked. ‌Modern ‌speakers ​should not ‌expect ​exact ​identity ​with ancient ‌phonology; ​the ​reconstruction ​is a ‌scholarly ​compass, ​not ​a performance ‌prescription. ​The ‌restoration ​Maitreya ‌keeps the ​prosodic ‌information ‌visible ​even when ​the ​name ​is ‌typed in ‌plain ​ASCII.

mythology.body:
The ​stories of ‌Maitreya ‌place future ​buddha, ​loving-kindness at ​the ​center of ​a ‌living mythological ​world.

​### Origins ‌(Myth)

​Maitreya appears ‌in ​buddhist tradition ‌as ​future buddha, ​loving-kindness. ​The name's ​meaning, ​"'The Benevolent ‌One' — ​the ‌Bodhisattva who ​will ‌return as ​the ‌future Buddha", ​shapes ‌the narratives ​told ​about this ‌figure.

‌### Worship ‌and ​Memory (Cult)

​Devotees ‌and later ​tradition-keepers ​preserved Maitreya ‌in ​ritual, text, ​and ‌iconography, ensuring ​the ‌name survived ​into ​the modern ​scholarly ​record.

The ‌myths ‌of Maitreya ​survive ‌in fragments, ​summaries, ​and later ‌retellings. ‌Each version ‌reflects ‌the interests ​of ‌its tellers ​— ​poets, priests, ​philosophers, ‌and scholars. ​The PuniCodex ​entry ​does not ‌privilege ​a single ​version; ​it gathers ‌the ​attestations so ‌that ​readers can ‌compare ​them. The ‌restoration ‌Maitreya gives ​the ​figure a ​stable ​name around ‌which ‌these variants ​orbit.

archaeology.body:
No ​monument, ‌inscription, ‌or artifact ​in ​the ​current ​PuniCodex ​corpus ‌is ​yet assigned ​to ‌Maitreya ​with ‌certainty. ​That ‌absence ​should be ​read ​honestly: ​for ​a ‌Buddhist ​name ‌of this ​type ‌the ​material ‌record ​is ‌expected to ​be ​thin, ‌and ‌the ‌primary ​evidence ​remains the ‌textual ​testimony ​gathered ‌in ​the ​Scholarly ‌Sources section.

​Were ‌such ​evidence ​to ​surface, ​it ‌would take ‌recognizable ​forms: ‌votive ​or ​dedicatory ‌inscriptions ‌naming मैत्रेय, ‌sanctuary ‌or ​cult ‌remains ​tied ​to future ​buddha ‌and ​iconography ​matching ​its ‌traditional ​attributes (name ​and ​domain). ‌Each ​candidate ‌would ​be ‌weighed against ​the ‌reconstructed ‌form ​of ​the ​name ​before entering ‌the ‌scholarly ​record.

meditation.body:
To ​contemplate Maitreya ‌is ‌to hold ​the ​idea of ​future ​Buddha, ​Loving-Kindness in ‌the ​mind and ​to ‌ask what ​of ‌it endures. ​The ‌name means ​"'The ​Benevolent One' ​— ​the Bodhisattva ​who ‌will ​return as ‌the ​future Buddha" ‌— ​and a ‌name ​that carries ‌its ​meaning so ​openly ‌invites meditation ‌rather ‌than mere ​recollection. ​The ‌tradition remembers ​the ​name as ‌future ​Buddha, Loving-Kindness ​· ‌'The Benevolent ​One' ‌— the ​Bodhisattva ​who will ​return ​as the ‌future ‌Buddha.

​Sit with ‌the ​restored form ​— ‌Maitreya — ‌and ‌the diacritics ‌themselves ​become the ‌practice: ​each mark ​is ​a small ‌act ​of ​attention, a ​refusal ‌to let ​the ​plain ASCII ​form ‌*maitreya* stand ​in ‌for the ​whole. ‌What the ​tradition ‌preserved in ‌this ​name, ​the restoration ​asks ​the reader ‌to ‌preserve in ​turn.
